# PR #167 round 4 correctness verdict

**PASS-WITH-NOTES** at `afa8659318d1663dd9af27e5f24be5d91ba65b00`.

**F004 is closed. All four reviewer findings are now closed.** The new wake authorization checks the higher-sequence pending row atomically, preserving the older compaction's fallback rather than prematurely superseding it.

## F004 closure

mark_compaction_woken performs one owned UPDATE that requires the target row to be pending and rejects it when a higher-seq pending row of the **same seat** exists. Both outer references are explicitly qualified as compaction_wakes.seat/seq; the subquery does not compare the newer row to itself.

This check is inside the write transaction, not another pre-mark snapshot. A newer tracking row committed before the mark is therefore considered even if the watchdog's earlier pending list did not contain it.

The daemon uses this method only for Step::Wake. False or error skips wake entirely; a veto changes no row, so A remains pending. Other settlement paths retain their existing semantics.

The new real-store regression exercises the requested boundary: read A, commit B, reject A's mark and verify Some(None), add a higher-seq row of another seat, settle B undelivered, then permit A exactly once. This proves same-seat isolation, pending-state filtering, preserved fallback and duplicate-mark exclusion.
